newsitem.title: USA: KC Fed's Hoenig sees U.S. GDP growth of 2-2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: KC Fed's Hoenig sees U.S. GDP growth of 2-2.5 pct.

text.p: Thomas Hoenig, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, on Thursday reiterated the central bank's forecast for U.S. gross domestic product growth in the range of 2 to 2.5 percent during the coming year.
The economy advanced by 3.4 percent in 1996 on a fourth-quarter to fourth-quarter basis.
Hoenig predicted that 1997 would be a "good year" for the economy overall, and said he expected healthy demand for U.S. exports.
He said the consumer sector looked healthy and said spending would be supported by income gains as the economy continues to add jobs.

"Business investment should also show solid gains," the Kansas City Fed chief said, adding that business inventories were at "fairly low" levels historically, which should give firms room to add to them.
Speaking at a luncheon sponsored by the Labor Management Council of Greater Kansas City, he also said he saw continued growth in manufacturing.
Hoenig stressed the Fed's commitment to promoting sustainable long-term growth but said the best way it could contribute to that would be by providing a stable price environment.
Asked during the question-and-answer session about what he thought the goals should be with regard to inflation, Hoenig said he would be cautious about providing a specific number.
Still, he suggested it would be useful for the Fed to look at the issue.
"I would like to see us evaluate a number that we could agree on but I think that's quite a process for several reasons," Hoenig said.
One issue is selecting among the various price indexes and there are also questions about the accuracy of the Consumer Price Index.
Speaking generally, Hoenig said, "I feel comfortable in the sense of inflation in the two percent range," but he said much would depend on the specific index that was chosen.
